cim: Új prompt útmutatót adott ki az OpenAI a GPT-6.2 Astra és Sol modellekhez
lead: Az OpenAI kész sablonokkal segíti a fejlesztőket a GPT-6.2 Astra és Sol modellek túl rövid válaszainak és felesleges kérdéseinek elkerülésében.
osszefoglalo:
Az OpenAI közzétette a legújabb **prompt sablonjait**, amelyek a GPT-6.2 Astra és Sol használata során felmerülő tipikus hibák kiküszöbölésére szolgálnak. Az új kiadások alapértelmezetten tömörebben fogalmaznak, mint a korábbi modellek, így a korábbi tanácsokkal ellentétben a fejlesztőknek érdemes elhagyniuk a leegyszerűsítésre vonatkozó utasításokat. A sablonok segítenek megakadályozni, hogy a modell feleslegesen kérdezzen vissza ahelyett, hogy önállóan elvégezné a feladatot.

A kódolási folyamatoknál a friss útmutatás arra ösztönzi a modelleket, hogy a meglévő kódbázist használják újra, ne hozzanak létre felesleges segédfüggvényeket, és csak a legszükségesebb esetekben írjanak új teszteket. Az OpenAI emellett a [Responses API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses) működését is módosította: a beszélgetési előzmények szerkesztésekor a modell elveszítheti a korábbi gondolkodási folyamat részleteit, ami ronthatja a válaszminőséget és növelheti a tokenfogyasztást.

A november 17-én megjelent GPT-6.2 Astra az API-n keresztül 8 dollárba kerül egymillió bemeneti tokenenként és 40 dollárba egymillió kimeneti tokenenként. A Sol modell a komplex feladatokat lényegesen alacsonyabb költség mellett végzi el.
miert_szamit: A GPT-6.2-re váltó fejlesztőknek érdemes **teljesen átnézniük a rendszerszintű utasításaikat**, mert a modell kevesebb kérdéssel és kevesebb felesleges tesztkóddal gyorsabb, olcsóbb munkafolyamatokat tesz lehetővé.

cim_eredeti: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
szoveg_eredeti:
OpenAI has released new prompt templates for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol covering writing style, initiative, and coding, alongside API changes that can discard reasoning content.

OpenAI says developers moving to GPT-6.2 Astra or Sol should review their system prompts. The company published copy-ready prompts in the models' documentation to curb behaviors it observed in both releases. Astra is built for the most demanding tasks, while Sol handles complex work at lower cost.

Astra writes more briefly and directly by default than earlier models, according to OpenAI. That means developers switching over should reconsider instructions like "be concise." For use as a colleague in everyday work, the company recommends a prompt that adopts user and source terminology, uses active voice, and puts key points first. When writing for external readers, the model should account for their lack of context. When editing, it should preserve the author's meaning and phrasing.

On long tasks, the model sometimes carries shorthand from its reasoning or other agents' messages into the final response. A dedicated prompt tells it to write that final answer so it stands on its own.

Treat your final answer as the user's first look at your work, and not as a continuation of intermediate commentary. The final answer must always be fully self-contained: users should never need to read earlier commentary updates for context, since they are collapsed when the final answer is shown to the user.

Write the final answer and all other human-facing material anew for the intended reader. Do not copy or closely paraphrase your reasoning or adopt its writing style. Do not carry over working shorthand, jargon, or abbreviations from your reasoning, tool calls, or instructions to subagents and automations.

When user intent is unclear, GPT-6.2 sometimes suggests a next step and waits for confirmation, OpenAI says. The company recommends a prompt telling the model to carry out those steps itself whenever it is authorized to do so. It should pause only for a major change in task scope, a real blocker, a decision the user must make, or an irreversible or destructive action.

When details are unclear, the model should make reversible assumptions, flag them, and keep working. Higher reasoning effort also helps it follow through on final checks during long tasks, OpenAI adds.

Avoid stopping to end the turn while the task is incomplete or if there is an authorized next step you can take, and instead take the next steps within task scope to progress the user's request. If your final response before ending the turn is a suggested next step, a plan, a request to the user for a routine decision, instructions for a task to execute, or similar handoff to the user, take these steps yourself to make progress towards what the user asked for. Make sure that you have authorization to do so, and flag any assumptions or decisions you make to the user.

Only stop to clarify with the user if there is significant change in task scope, you are concretely blocked, have a decision that the user needs to resolve, or before irreversible or destructive actions.

OpenAI says GPT-6.2 writes more efficient code than its predecessors. Its template instructs the model to reuse existing logic and avoid unnecessary helper functions, while adding new tests only when requested, required by the repo, or needed to catch specific regressions. Fewer lines and shorter variable names are not a substitute for simplicity.

For frontends, developers should specify imagery and typography directly. By default, the template favors realistic images from image generation or search and uses SVGs only on request. Decorative numbering, filler badges, and helper text that only repeats what the interface already shows should be left out.
